handle.description: The operator's handle for this agent (compose service, logs, CLI, session keys). The agent chooses its own name on first boot.

description.description: One line: what job this agent does. Also shown to the agent during the naming ritual.

provider.description: LLM provider dialect. openai-compatible covers OpenAI, Ollama, vLLM, and any compatible proxy. codex uses an OpenAI Codex (ChatGPT) subscription via the credentials from `codex login` (no API key).

id.description: Model identifier, e.g. gpt-5.4-mini or claude-sonnet-5.

small.description: Model for cheap internal calls (summaries, compaction, the naming ritual). Defaults to the main model.

base_url.description: Endpoint override, e.g. http://localhost:11434/v1 for Ollama with openai-compatible (no API key required with a base_url).

api_key_env.description: Name of the env var holding the API key — a reference, never a value. Defaults to OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY per provider.

fallbacks.description: Model ids to fall back to when the primary fails.

model.description: Which model runs this agent, and how to reach it.

purpose.description: The agent's job description — what it does, how it behaves, when to stay quiet. Becomes the model's system prompt.

triggers.description: Event sources that wake the agent. With triggers, `af run` starts a long-lived service; without, an interactive REPL.

channels.description: Channel names or ids to listen in; omit for all channels the bot can see. DMs always pass.

require_mention.description: Only respond when the bot is @-mentioned. DMs always address the bot.

token_env.description: Env var holding the Discord bot token.

from_users.description: Only handle messages from these authors (user ids or usernames); the filter runs before the model is called. Omit for anyone.

reply_channel.description: Channel id to post replies into instead of the source channel. Out-of-channel replies quote the triggering message and link back.

allow_silence.description: Post nothing when the agent replies with exactly __NO_REPLY__ (or nothing). Instruct the sentinel in purpose.

show_typing.description: Show the typing indicator in the source channel while the agent works. Looks odd with allow_silence: typing may end in no message.

oneOf.description: Listen to Discord messages via the gateway; replies go in-channel by default.

channels.description: Channel names or ids to listen in; omit for all channels the bot is in.

require_mention.description: Only respond when the bot is @-mentioned. DMs always address the bot.

token_env.description: Env var holding the bot token (xoxb-…) — reads channel info, posts replies.

app_token_env.description: Env var holding the app-level token (xapp-…, scope connections:write) for Socket Mode.

from_users.description: Only handle messages from these Slack user ids (U…); the filter runs before the model is called. Omit for anyone.

reply_channel.description: Channel id to post replies into instead of the source thread. Out-of-channel replies quote the triggering message and link back.

allow_silence.description: Post nothing when the agent replies with exactly __NO_REPLY__ (or nothing). Instruct the sentinel in purpose.

oneOf.description: Listen to Slack messages via Socket Mode (no public endpoint); replies go in-thread by default.

chats.description: Chat ids, group titles, or public @usernames to listen in; omit for all chats the bot sees.

require_mention.description: Only respond when the bot is @-mentioned. Private chats always address the bot.

token_env.description: Env var holding the bot token from @BotFather.

from_users.description: Only handle messages from these authors (user ids or usernames); the filter runs before the model is called. Omit for anyone.

reply_chat.description: Chat id to post replies into instead of the source chat. Out-of-chat replies quote the triggering message and link back.

allow_silence.description: Post nothing when the agent replies with exactly __NO_REPLY__ (or nothing). Instruct the sentinel in purpose.

oneOf.description: Listen to Telegram messages via Bot API long-polling (no public endpoint); replies go in-chat by default.

token_env.description: Env var holding the bearer token callers must present. Required: an unauthenticated endpoint contradicts deny-by-default.

oneOf.description: HTTP trigger: POST {path} with authorization: Bearer <token> and JSON body {input, conversation_id?}; responds with the run result.

transport.description: How mail arrives. resend is the pushed transport: Resend receives mail for your domain and POSTs each message here as a signed webhook.

path.description: HTTP path the provider POSTs inbound-mail webhooks to.

signing_secret_env.description: Env var holding the webhook signing secret (whsec_…). Every request is verified before parsing; unsigned POSTs get a 401.

api_key_env.description: Env var holding the Resend API key — fetches message bodies and sends replies.

from_addresses.description: Senders the agent handles: exact addresses or *@domain patterns. Required — an email address is open to the whole internet. ["*"] accepts anyone, stated in the file that defines the agent's reach.

allow_silence.description: Send nothing when the agent replies with exactly __NO_REPLY__ (or nothing). Instruct the sentinel in purpose.

oneOf.description: Wake on inbound email delivered by Resend's email.received webhook; replies go back out through the Resend API in the same thread.

transport.description: How mail arrives. imap is the pulled transport for an existing mailbox: the trigger polls the folder for unseen messages and replies over SMTP.

username.description: Mailbox login — also the address replies are sent from.

password_env.description: Env var holding the mailbox password (an app password where the provider requires one).

smtp_host.description: SMTP server for replies, e.g. smtp.fastmail.com.

folder.description: Folder to watch. The unseen flag is the cursor — handled and dropped messages are marked seen — so give the agent a folder it owns.

from_addresses.description: Senders the agent handles: exact addresses or *@domain patterns. Required. ["*"] accepts anyone.

allow_silence.description: Send nothing when the agent replies with exactly __NO_REPLY__ (or nothing). Instruct the sentinel in purpose.

oneOf.description: Wake on unseen messages in an IMAP mailbox; replies go out over SMTP in the same thread.

transport.description: How mail arrives. gmail polls the Gmail API for unread messages in a label, authenticated by an OAuth refresh token.

client_id.description: OAuth client id of your Google Cloud project's Desktop-app client.

client_secret_env.description: Env var holding the OAuth client secret.

refresh_token_env.description: Env var holding the refresh token from the one-time consent flow (docs/email.mdx documents it).

label.description: Gmail label to watch. The unread state is the cursor — handled and dropped messages are marked read — so route mail here with Gmail filters and let the agent own the label.

from_addresses.description: Senders the agent handles: exact addresses or *@domain patterns. Required. ["*"] accepts anyone.

allow_silence.description: Send nothing when the agent replies with exactly __NO_REPLY__ (or nothing). Instruct the sentinel in purpose.

oneOf.description: Wake on unread Gmail messages in a label via the Gmail API; replies land in the same Gmail thread.

transport.description: How mail arrives. outlook polls Microsoft Graph for unread messages in a folder, authenticated by an OAuth refresh token.

client_id.description: Client id of your Entra app registration.

client_secret_env.description: Env var holding the client secret — confidential clients only. Public (device-code) clients omit this.

refresh_token_env.description: Env var holding the refresh token from the one-time device-code flow (docs/email.mdx documents it).

tenant.description: Entra tenant: "common", "consumers", "organizations" or a tenant id.

folder.description: Mail folder to watch: a well-known name (inbox) or a folder id. The unread state is the cursor — handled and dropped messages are marked read.

from_addresses.description: Senders the agent handles: exact addresses or *@domain patterns. Required. ["*"] accepts anyone.

allow_silence.description: Send nothing when the agent replies with exactly __NO_REPLY__ (or nothing). Instruct the sentinel in purpose.

oneOf.description: Wake on unread Outlook messages in a folder via Microsoft Graph; replies land in the same conversation.
Wake on inbound email. transport picks how mail arrives: resend (pushed webhooks for the agent's own address), or imap / gmail / outlook (poll an existing mailbox).

prompt.description: What to tell the agent each tick.

oneOf.description: Fire the agent on a schedule with a fixed prompt.

items.description: An event source that wakes the agent.

skills.description: Paths to skill markdown files (relative to this config). Skills carry knowledge, never capability.

tools.description: Tool sources beyond the natives and skills.

mcp.description: MCP servers to connect at startup.

name.description: Server name; its tools appear namespaced as mcp__<name>__<tool>.

command.description: stdio server: argv to launch it, e.g. [docker, run, -i, ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server].

env.description: Env vars passed to the server — values may be ${VAR} references. The server sees only these (scoped, no ambient inheritance).

include.description: Expose only these tools. Strongly recommended: a fat server must not blow a small model's context.

readonly.description: Expose only tools whose readOnlyHint annotation marks them read-only. A guard against wiring write tools into a read-only job; the hint is self-reported by the server.

items.description: A Model Context Protocol server providing tools to the agent.

custom.description: Paths to custom TypeScript tool modules. Not yet implemented (issue #12).

search.description: Tool search: defer MCP tool schemas out of context behind a search_tools tool. auto defers when the agent has more than 10 tools; on always defers; off loads everything.

net.description: Hosts http_request may reach; *.example.com matches subdomains (not the apex).

run.description: Executables run_bash may spawn, matched by basename. run_bash exists only if this grants something.

permissions.description: Deny-by-default allowlists. Omitting this block means the agent can touch nothing; denials are surfaced to the model as tool results.

env.description: Env for tools and MCP servers. Values may be ${VAR} references, resolved at startup (env var, then /run/secrets/<VAR>) and scoped per tool.

scope.description: thread: conversation history persists per conversation key (chat channel or thread, webhook conversation_id). none: every run starts fresh.

persistent.description: Give the agent remember/recall/list_memories/forget tools backed by its own SQLite file — facts and preferences that survive across conversation keys and restarts, not just one thread's history.

memory.description: What the agent remembers between events.

max_steps.description: Tool-calling iterations (LLM calls) per run. On hitting the cap the agent gets one final tool-less call to summarize its progress, then the run ends with error_max_steps.

limits.description: Per-run budgets — the dead-man's switches for unattended operation.

description: A Looped AF agent: one job, one file. https://github.com/loopedautomation/agent-framework
